# Pinned original Hermes tool-message fixture

These are the reviewed, unchanged AST fragments and a closed driver adapted from
NousResearch/hermes-agent commit `749cb638ff43f9ce5333c186a1e4f67d473aa4f2`.
The original MIT notice is retained. Source receipts and fragment provenance record
exact public source bytes. Whole cached upstream modules are deliberately not copied.

The driver executes original assistant call/message constructors, original supplied
result-message construction, sanitizer helpers and explicitly selected append/API
cleanup statements. Its synthetic SDK-like objects, argument strings, result values,
ordering and collaborators are disclosed by every capture. It does not execute an
actual tool, the complete Hermes API/commit pipeline, an SDK serializer or a provider.
The repeated-ID cases prove constructor preservation, not gateway authorization.

`decision-application-tools.test.ts` combines those projected messages with the
separately pinned original kwargs builder and declared streaming flags. This is
synthetic real-handler protocol acceptance, not an installed Hermes client or live
model-quality/entitlement result. No secret, private configuration or screenshot is
included in this fixture.

The local runner adds only a bounded synthetic `tool_name` input passed to the
unchanged original constructors. This aligns the message fixture with the
separately executed original kwargs builder's declared tool. It changes no
upstream fragment or argument/result processing and is disclosed in capture
substitutions. No real tool is run.

The legacy `agent_fixture()` capture keeps its closed synthetic ID collaborators. The separate installed-SDK fixture calls `agent_fixture(pinned_ids=True)`: it executes only the two exact hash-checked original ID helper bodies recorded in `tool-id-fragments.json` and `tool-id-provenance.json`, from the same pinned Hermes revision. It does not import their original adapter module or add Codex execution support. The unused random-ID fallback remains a failing canary. This allows legitimate gateway correlation IDs without renaming them to fit a stub.
